Row.Text: [B]Yemen[/B] is able to endure throughout the Ages.
Merchant from all over the world traded in [B]Yemen[/B].

After months of travelling, a merchant finally arrive in a {1_Civilization_Adj} market. Someone is trading spices for pearls, another is exchanging ebony for fine textiles. The abundance of the world can be seen here, each corner revealing new treasures from far away. The merchant settles down and prepares their table, certain of the new goods they will acquire.

Our strategic position in the incense trade attracts settlers from beyond the horizon. The frankincense and myrrh trees are a source of wealth making {1_Civilization_Adj} rulers the dominant economic force in the region. But the abundance of gold doesn't corrupt them, as the smell of incense inspire them instead to study God's creation.

The date palm tree, like {1_Civilization_Adj} tribes here, is able to flourish in the harshest part of the desert. More than a simple fruit, the date enable the {1_Civilization_Adj}s to settle where no other went before and to establish cruicial stop points to whoever dares to travels through the desert to search new riches.
[B]Yemen[/B] had close trading ties with the [B]Mughals[/B].
